messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: GPU-pool-eu-west saturated > 95% queue growth detected. Pager duty triggered for oncall: maya. Priority: P1.

maya (oncall): on it — joining call in 2. seeing sustained enqueue rate spike, autoscaler not launching additional nodes.

eli (infra): adding context: autoscaler logs show repeated ScaleUpRejected errors: "scale limit reached for tenant-pools". Looks like a hard cap at 120 GPUs for eu-west.

sam (sre): queue backlog trending: +8k requests over 10m, 99th latency for queued requests is 45s and rising. Customer-facing rate limiting will kick in soon.

nora (runtime): per-request telemetry shows many requests are long-context (4k tokens) — KV cache miss rate high, batching inefficient. Could cause slower throughput.

maya (oncall): quick mitigations: 1) Enable emergency-limit-burst (if available) 2) Pause non-critical scheduled jobs 3) Route tier-3 customers to fallbacks. Who can flip those?

eli (infra): I can toggle burst via ops-bot. Executing: /ops-bot enable-burst eu-west --reason "incident 2165432100"

ops-bot: Command acknowledged. Burst capacity request submitted to provider. Expected spin-up 4–6 minutes. (reacted with :hourglass_flowing_sand:).

jamie (customer-success): heads-up: 3 enterprise customers in eu-west are showing elevated error rates — I'm preparing a short outbound with ETA. Any mitigation that reduces errors quickly is priority.

sam (sre): while we wait for burst, suggestion: apply temporary strict per-API-key qps caps for experimental routes to stabilize queue. maya, can you approve?

maya (oncall): approve. Apply caps to routes: /v1/generate-experimental, /v1/batch-eval. Keep other production routes untouched.

nora (runtime): rolling out runtime config change: disable large-compile-optimizations on burst nodes to reduce warm-up. Patch: ```PATCH /runtime/config
{"kv_cache.enabled": true, "batch.max_tokens": 512, "pileup_protection": "on"}``` Deploying to eu-west dev ring then canary.

eli (infra): burst nodes reported as PROVISIONING -> ACTIVE. Provider reports 16 GPUs provisioning.

sam (sre): monitor: queue slope reduced after qps caps, slow decline but stable. 10m backlog growth -> now 1m backlog reduction. Good signal.

ops-bot: Burst capacity ACTIVE: 16 GPUs added to eu-west pool.

maya (oncall): confirming autoscaler logs: still seeing ScaleUpRejected for reserved-pools due to per-tenant limit. We temporarily increased global capacity but reserved-tenant caps block further autoscale. Need follow-up.

eli (infra): noted. Creating short-lived override for reserved-pools to allow extra nodes for 1h: /ops-bot override-tenant-limit reserved-pools +20 --ttl 3600

ops-bot: Override created for reserved-pools (+20 GPUs) ttl 3600s.

sam (sre): backlog now decreasing steadily, 99th latency back to ~12s. Some individual requests still timing out (clients with no retry). We should publish guidance to customers recommending retry/backoff.

jamie (customer-success): Sent escalation note to affected enterprise contacts with recommended mitigations (retry with exponential backoff, shorter context where possible).

nora (runtime): observed a separate issue: the autoscaler backoff code does exponentialBackoff up to 10m but a bug prevents reattempts when ScaleUpRejected returns specific error code 429_PROVIDER_CAP. We'll need a patch.

maya (oncall): capture action items and assign owners. Current on-call will continue stabilization. After that, postmortem by this week.

sam (sre): Live mitigation summary so far: - Enabled burst capacity (+16 GPUs) - Applied tenant override (+20 GPUs) - Throttled experimental routes - Deployed runtime batching guards - Notified customers.

nora (runtime): immediate root cause hypothesis: combination of skewed request mix (long contexts), autoscaler hitting configured hard caps per-tenant, and autoscaler logic that treats ScaleUpRejected as terminal rather than retryable.

eli (infra): temporary fix: extend per-tenant caps and add provider quotas to our monitoring alerts. Permanent fix: negotiate higher provider quota + implement smarter scaling fallback.

maya (oncall): any customer impact notes? jamie?

jamie (customer-success): Impact: 3 enterprise customers in eu-west had elevated error rates for ~22 minutes. We provided mitigation steps and temporary credits. No SLA breaches confirmed yet, but one support ticket opened.

sam (sre): timeline: Incident opened 2165432100 -> burst active 2165432320 -> tenant override 2165432400 -> queue stable by 2165432500 -> incident declared mitigated at 2165432600.

maya (oncall): closing note: I'll file an incident report and schedule postmortem. Preliminary action items: 1) Fix autoscaler retry logic for ScaleUpRejected (owner: nora) 2) Raise per-tenant hard cap and add guardrails (owner: eli) 3) Add playbook entry for emergency-burst + override (owner: sam) 4) Improve customer alert templates for capacity events (owner: jamie) 5) Add telemetry for context-length distribution to alert earlier (owner: nora).

nora (runtime): acknowledged. I'll open the PR for autoscaler retry within today and include unit tests.

eli (infra): I'll schedule provider quota request and add dashboard panels for per-tenant cap usage.

sam (sre): will write the incident timeline and craft the mitigation runbook update.

jamie (customer-success): I'll follow up with customers and close out tickets after postmortem.

maya (oncall): thanks team. incident status -> mitigated. please add any missing notes to the thread. (reacted with :white_check_mark:)

ops-bot: Incident 2165432100 marked mitigated by maya at ts 2165432600. Postmortem required within 72 hours.

sam (sre): quick post-incident observation: consider short-term limit on 4k-token requests during peak windows via product quota. Might reduce these escalations.

nora (runtime): agreed — proposing adaptive context caps per-customer for the next iteration of Optimize.

maya (oncall): good. I'll include that as an advisory in the postmortem. Closing thread.

(End of thread)
